Learn the class by solving it

“Black Friday Rescue” is a game about Thursday's class: six missions at Mercadillo 505 and a final level. You can play it alone, without the professor. This guide shows every step with short animations.

💻A browser — Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari
📴No internet, nothing to install
⏱25–35 minutes
✅Formative — not graded
1

Start the game and find the map

  1. Open IT505_Class04_Game_Black_Friday_Rescue.html in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. No internet and no installation are needed.
  2. Type your first name if you like (it only appears on your certificate) and press Start the game ▶.
  3. The map shows six missions and a final level. The yellow circle is your next mission; green means done; 🔒 means locked.
Want to revise one topic only? Press 🔓 Free mode below the map: every mission opens.
2

Play a mission — always the same four steps

  1. 1 · The problem — read the situation at Mercadillo 505. Do not look for the answer yet.
  2. 2 · Try it first — solve a small challenge with your own head: sort, predict, click, mine, decide. Mistakes are explained, never punished.
  3. 3 · The principle — the idea behind your challenge, the slides of the lecture with the professor's notes, and short videos.
  4. 4 · Lock it in — flash-cards and a quick check. Then Complete the mission ✓.
This is “problem first”: you meet the question before the tool, the way engineers learn a new idea.
3

Example — Mission 2: map, shuffle, reduce

  1. Eighteen orders sit on three machines. Press MAP, SHUFFLE and REDUCE in the order you think is right.
  2. Pressed the wrong one? The game explains why that phase cannot come yet. Try again.
  3. At the end, one question about the city names — then Next.
4

Example — Mission 5: find the changed block, then try to hide it

  1. Press check on the blocks: green means the stored hash still matches; red means the record was changed.
  2. Click the block you accuse. Then play the dishonest insider: Re-hash blocks until the chain is valid again.
  3. Count your re-hashes: hiding one change means rewriting every later block.
The hashes are real SHA-256, computed in your browser — the same algorithm as Lab 2.
5

Example — Mission 6: mine a block, then decide

  1. Press ⛏ Mine: your browser tries one nonce after another until the hash starts with 000.
  2. Answer the question about the cost of one more zero.
  3. Run three company proposals through the six yes/no questions; the flowchart gives the verdict.
6

The library and the final level

  1. 📚 Library (top right, always available): lessons in short, all 55 slides with notes, all flash-cards, every question, Lab 2 as animations, videos, links, abbreviations, legal notice.
  2. 🏆 Final level: ten mixed questions after the six missions. Then your certificate of practice: print it or save it as PDF if you like.

Questions

Does the game count towards my grade?

No. Everything in it is formative practice: nothing is graded, recorded or sent anywhere.

Is my progress saved?

Yes, in this browser only (its local storage). Another browser or computer starts from zero; “Reset progress” clears it.

How long does it take?

About 25 to 35 minutes for the six missions and the final level. You can stop at any time and come back.

Do I need the internet?

No. Only the video links and the official links open web pages; check each link first with its ✓VT button (VirusTotal).

Can I play on a phone?

Yes, but a laptop or a tablet is more comfortable: the challenges have many buttons.

A challenge seems stuck.

Read the yellow or red message under it: it says what is missing. You can also press “Start again” in Mission 1 or go back to the map and reopen the mission.

What does it have to do with Lab 2?

Missions 1–4 practise Part A (Scale), Mission 5 practises Part B (Seal), Mission 6 practises Part C (Decide). The library shows every Lab 2 step as an animation.
